alignments.note: Waw takes the connective left over after עַתָּה takes the word writing its own lexeme (rule 14).
Discourse adverb takes Now, the word writing its own lexeme (rule 14).
Imperative keeps only its own lexical verb; the pronoun written after it is objective and is placed separately below.

Corrected from the accepted reading, which kept you with the imperative on rule 36's adjacency sentence. That sentence allocates a single ye or thou between a verb and a vocative standing in the same clause, and no vocative stands here; and the word is ASV objective you in indirect-object position, not the nominative ye that would realize the imperative's own person and number under rule 17 (contrast come ye down at 1SA.6.21). It is a benefactive dative the Hebrew does not write — no לְ and no suffix stands on עֲשׂוּ — so no morpheme licenses it and rule 44's supplied-pronoun clause makes it its own added unit under rule 30.
Noun with the indefinite article it licenses (rule 15), discontinuous around the attributive.

The ASV writes no one for this numeral; the a is the noun's own under rule 15, since the Hebrew writes a noun for the numeral to count. Giving the a to the numeral is the competing reading, which rule 15 reserves for a substantival numeral.
Relative; the ASV writes two words for relative and preposition, so rule 2 splits them (rule 22).
The clause's negation is recast as the determiner on the noun, and the negative takes it (rule 15).
Finite verb with presentative dummy and auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
Preposition takes the on written for it.
Resumptive suffix left unwritten beside a separately rendered relative and preposition (rule 22).
Object marker with no English of its own (rule 16).
Assimilated article token takes the written the (rule 12).

Source head corrected from s032. MACULA tags both morphemes R, so this is a compound preposition written from two prepositions, not a preposition on a construct noun: neither morpheme carries content the other lacks, since the one English word from carries the pair, so rule 23's syntactic-head sentence governs and the head is the morpheme standing first, exactly as מֵעַל → from does there and as מֵעָלֵינוּ does at 1SA.6.20 in this chapter. Rule 23 also forbids moving the head onto the morpheme whose own sense the English word happens to write.
Suffix takes its own pronoun; it is no part of the fusion (rule 30's rider).

The article, noun and directive he jointly render home, the definite spatial adverb expressly covered by rules 30 and 32. The noun carries the lexical head. Leaving the article unrepresented applies the ordinary article rule without its current spatial-adverb exception.

review_notes: Corrected two units. The source head of מֵאַחֲרֵי moves to the מִן: both morphemes are tagged R, so rule 23's compound-preposition sentence governs and the head is the one standing first, as it is for מֵעָלֵינוּ at 1SA.6.20.

The you of prepare you a new cart is now its own added unit: it is objective, not the nominative ye rule 17 would give the imperative, no dative morpheme stands in the Hebrew for it, and rule 36's adjacency sentence requires a vocative in the clause, which there is none.
